prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities and monetary policy rules, which underpin the New Keynesian framework used in modern monetary policy analysis.

statement.case_for: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the conceptual basis of how monetary policy is modelled and conducted. Calvo's time-dependent pricing, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's microfounded policy framework are three separable, identifiable contributions. They are not simply one paper split three ways. The framework has been tested across several decades and through the post-2008 and post-2021 episodes, so its record can be assessed. It also links theory to institutional practice, in the sense that the policy rule and the optimal-policy analysis changed what central banks do. That is a meaningful standard of influence under criteria applied equally across fields. Having reread the openings, I keep B012 first, but with less confidence in the attribution than in the scientific significance.
statement.case_against: Credit is spread across at least eight people. Any three-person cut leaves out Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets or Gertler, whose quantitative and empirical contributions are arguably part of why the framework became operational. The framework's performance after 2008 and in the 2021-23 inflation is contested. Taylor's rule is partly an empirical regularity rather than a deep theoretical result. Earlier prizes (Phelps, Lucas, Sargent and Sims, Kydland and Prescott, Bernanke) overlap in subject, so the incremental claim has to be argued explicitly. The attribution problem is the strongest reservation, and B026 has a cleaner credit structure.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B012 first with Taylor, Calvo and Woodford, but notes that the Taylor rule is a rule of thumb more than a deep theoretical result, so some may weigh it less than Calvo's and Woodford's contributions.
responses.response: I agree the rule is less deep theoretically than Woodford's framework, and I take that as a real qualification. I still include Taylor. His staggered-contracts model is a separate conceptual contribution, and the rule is what connected the theory to measurable central-bank behaviour and a testable policy benchmark. If the Committee judged the rule too thin, the natural substitution would be Gali for the empirical and theoretical New Keynesian Phillips curve work. I would prefer that to dropping the policy-relevance dimension altogether.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B026 first. She argues that Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, that Helpman is a defensible second laureate and that Redding's work is more derivative, which gives a compact and durable credit structure.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my ordering, because B026 has much cleaner attribution than B012. I do not treat the number of members ranking either candidate highly as evidence of merit. On the substance, my remaining reservations about B026 are the overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize and the credit owed to Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, who are outside the ballot entry. I keep B012 first because its policy consequences are larger and its credit problem can be managed with three separable contributions. I name B026 as my first alternative because I would not regard it as a weak choice.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B007 first and proposes adding Gertler to Kiyotaki and Moore. He also stresses that the New Keynesian credit is diffuse and that Gertler's credit competes between B007 and B012.
responses.response: I share his concern about diffuse New Keynesian credit, and it is the main reason I hold B012 with reservations. On B007, I find the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism clear and well attributed to the original pair. I would keep it to two names because the financial-accelerator strand overlaps with the 2022 recognition of Bernanke. Adding Gertler would worsen the attribution problem that B012 already has. I rank B007 sixth because I see the 2022 overlap as costing it more than the foundational clarity of the mechanism gains it.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B009 first as the founding body of political economics. She notes that the Persson-Tabellini core is clear, that Besley is a close third, and that the 2024 prize may make the Committee cautious.
responses.response: I agree B009 is coherent and mature, and I ranked it second. I would not rank it first. My concern about adjacency to the 2024 institutions prize is real, and some of the cross-country constitutional estimates rest on weaker identification than the best causal work. I judge it a strong alternative, but I do not think it clearly outweighs the policy reach and conceptual centrality of the nominal-rigidities line.

uncertainties: Where to draw the line between the Calvo, Taylor and Woodford core and the estimation and empirical contributions of Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler.
Whether the 2021-23 inflation episode and heterogeneous-agent critiques should reduce confidence in the framework's empirical record.
How much the earlier macroeconomic and monetary prizes reduce the incremental case for a New Keynesian award.
Whether a cleaner-credit alternative such as B026 should outweigh B012's policy influence when the Committee decides.
statement.conflict_note: My profile lists a co-authored paper on corruption as a collective-action problem with a 'Persson' and Rothstein, but gives no first name, so I cannot establish from the supplied profile whether this is Torsten Persson. My opening note stating that Persson co-authored with me therefore overstated what the profile supports, and I withdraw it. If the person is the B009 candidate, this would be a connection relevant to B009, which is only an alternative here. My field is political science and I have long-standing ties to Swedish institutional research, including collaborators in quality-of-government work. I am a colleague at Stockholm University of other committee members, but in a different department. No connection to B012 candidates is apparent from the supplied profile.
